# Entropy Source Core — Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Overview

The entropy source core is the central control and datapath module of the entropy source IP. Its purpose is to:

- Collect raw randomness from an external physical RNG source.
- Perform continuous hardware health checks on the raw stream.
- Optionally condition the entropy using a SHA-3 based conditioner.
- Provide a firmware-override path for firmware-managed health testing and conditioning.
- Deliver complete 384-bit entropy seeds either to firmware through a register read interface or to a hardware consumer through a request/acknowledge interface.
- Report status, alerts, interrupts, and error information to the register interface.

The module shall operate correctly in several modes: bypass/boot-time mode, FIPS-compliant mode, and firmware-override mode.

---

## 2. Reset and Initial State

After reset:

- The module shall be disabled.
- Entropy collection shall not start.
- All internal entropy buffers, health-test counters, conditioning state, and delivery FIFOs shall be cleared.
- No entropy seed shall be delivered to firmware or to the hardware entropy interface.
- All interrupt outputs shall be inactive.
- No alert shall be asserted.
- The FIPS compliance indication associated with any entropy output shall be low.

The module shall begin normal operation only after firmware programs the required configuration and asserts the module enable.

---

## 3. Module Enable and Security-Sensitive Configuration

The module shall support a securely encoded enable/disable mechanism. The enable must be considered valid only when it has a legal encoded value.

### 3.1 Disabled Behavior

When the module is disabled:

- The RNG enable output shall be deasserted.
- Raw RNG samples shall not be accepted into the entropy pipeline.
- Health tests shall be cleared and held in reset.
- All entropy data in the post-health, pre-conditioning, bypass, conditioning, and final delivery stages shall be cleared.
- Software entropy reads shall return zero.
- Hardware entropy delivery shall not occur.
- Firmware-override observe and insertion paths shall be inactive.

### 3.2 Invalid Configuration Encoding

Several configuration fields are security-sensitive and use multi-bit encoded values. These include:

- Module enable
- FIPS enable
- Entropy data register enable
- RNG bit selection enable
- Firmware-override mode controls
- Entropy routing and type controls
- Threshold scope control

If any such field is programmed with an invalid encoding:

- The associated feature shall not be enabled.
- The module shall report a recoverable alert condition.
- The invalid-field status shall be visible to firmware through the recoverable alert status registers.

### 3.3 OTP Gating

The firmware read path and firmware-override path shall be gated by OTP-provided enable values.

- If the OTP disables firmware reads, software entropy reads shall not return entropy data.
- If the OTP disables firmware override, all firmware-override controls shall be ignored.

---

## 4. Operating Modes

### 4.1 Bypass / Boot-Time Mode

This is the default mode after reset. The module shall operate in bypass mode when FIPS mode is not enabled or when firmware explicitly routes bypass entropy to the software path.

In bypass mode:

- Health tests shall use the bypass threshold set and bypass window size.
- The SHA-3 conditioner shall not be used.
- Raw health-tested entropy shall be packed directly into 384-bit seed words.
- Delivered seeds shall not be marked FIPS-compliant.

### 4.2 FIPS-Compliant Mode

When FIPS mode is enabled:

- Health tests shall use the FIPS threshold set and FIPS window size.
- Raw health-tested entropy shall be passed through the internal SHA-3 conditioner.
- The conditioner shall generate 384-bit seed words.
- A seed shall be marked FIPS-compliant only if the module is operating in FIPS mode and the single-bit RNG selection feature is not enabled.

### 4.3 Firmware-Override Mode

Firmware override mode provides an alternate data path for firmware-managed entropy processing.

In firmware-override mode:

- Post-health-test entropy shall be captured into an observe FIFO.
- Firmware may read the observed entropy and perform its own health tests.
- Firmware may write processed entropy back into the entropy pipeline.
- If firmware insertion is enabled, firmware-written data shall be inserted into the pre-conditioning stage.
- Inserted firmware data shall not be subjected to the hardware health tests.
- The hardware conditioner may still be used after firmware insertion if the module is not in bypass mode.

---

## 5. Raw Entropy Intake

The module shall receive raw entropy samples from the external RNG interface.

### 5.1 RNG Enable

- The RNG enable output shall be asserted when the module is enabled.
- When the module is disabled, the RNG enable output shall be deasserted.

### 5.2 Sample Acceptance

- Raw samples shall be accepted only while the module is enabled.
- Samples received while disabled shall be ignored.
- Accepted samples shall be placed in a small input buffer.
- If an accepted sample arrives while the input buffer is full, the sample shall be dropped and a fatal error shall be reported.
- If a buffer read occurs while the buffer is empty, or if the buffer reports an inconsistent full/empty state, a fatal error shall be reported.

### 5.3 Single-Bit Selection

The module may be configured to select one bit from each raw multi-bit sample instead of using the entire sample.

When single-bit selection is enabled:

- Only the selected bit of each sample shall be used for health testing and further processing.
- The module shall not mark final seeds as FIPS-compliant, even if FIPS mode is otherwise enabled.

---

## 6. Health Testing

The module shall perform the following health tests on the raw entropy stream:

- Repetition count test
- Repetition count symbol test
- Adaptive proportion test
- Bucket test
- Markov test
- Optional external vendor health test

Each test may be individually enabled or disabled by configuration.

### 6.1 General Health-Test Behavior

- Health tests shall observe the raw entropy stream and produce pass/fail indications.
- Each enabled test shall have programmable thresholds for both FIPS mode and bypass mode.
- The module shall select the threshold set that matches the current operating mode.
- Adaptive proportion and Markov tests shall support both aggregate and per-bit-lane threshold scope. The behavior shall follow the programmed threshold scope.
- The bucket test shall classify each multi-bit sample into a symbol bucket and count the distribution within a window.

### 6.2 Windows

- The repetition count test shall operate continuously, not on a fixed window.
- All other health tests shall operate over a fixed window of raw samples.
- The window size shall be selected according to the current operating mode:
  - FIPS mode uses the FIPS window size.
  - Bypass mode uses the bypass window size.
- At the end of each window, the module shall generate an internal window-done indication so that window-based tests can evaluate their counts.

### 6.3 External Health Test Interface

The module shall extend its health-testing capability to an optional external health-test block through a dedicated interface.

The module shall provide to the external block:

- The current raw entropy sample.
- A valid indication for the sample.
- The active/enable state of the external test.
- A clear signal to reset external test counters.
- The high and low threshold values.
- The configured window size.

The module shall accept from the external block:

- A test count result.
- High-threshold fail pulses.
- Low-threshold fail pulses.

External test failure pulses shall be treated identically to internal health-test failures for failure accounting, alert generation, and interrupt generation.

### 6.4 Failure Accounting

Every health-test fail event shall increment:

- The total fail counter for the specific test.
- A per-test alert fail counter.
- An aggregate alert failure counter.

The counters shall be cleared when:

- The module is disabled.
- A health-test clear is asserted.
- An explicit alert-counter reset is issued.

The module shall track whether a window contained at least one failure. This information shall be used by the control logic when evaluating alert thresholds and deciding whether to report a health-test alert.

### 6.5 Health-Test Alert Threshold

The module shall support a programmable alert threshold for health-test failures.

- If the aggregate failure count reaches the programmed alert threshold, a recoverable alert shall be asserted.
- If the alert threshold is programmed to zero, alert generation from the threshold shall be disabled.
- An inverted version of the alert threshold shall also be programmed. If the two programmed threshold encodings are inconsistent, the module shall report a recoverable alert.
- When the health-test alert condition is asserted, the module shall also assert the health-test-failed interrupt.

---

## 7. Firmware-Override Observe Path

In firmware-override mode, post-health-test entropy shall be captured into an observe FIFO so firmware can monitor or process it.

### 7.1 Observe FIFO Behavior

- The observe FIFO shall store 32-bit post-health-test words.
- The module shall expose the current FIFO depth to firmware.
- A programmable threshold shall be supported.
- When the FIFO depth reaches or exceeds the programmed threshold, and the threshold is nonzero, and the module is enabled, the module shall assert the observe-FIFO-ready interrupt.
- When the observe FIFO is full, incoming data shall be dropped.
- An overflow status shall be set whenever a valid post-health-test word is dropped because the observe FIFO is full.
- After an overflow, the FIFO shall stop accepting new data until it has been drained. This preserves contiguity of the captured entropy stream.
- Reading from the observe FIFO when it is empty shall report a fatal error.

### 7.2 Firmware Insertion

When firmware insertion is enabled in firmware-override mode:

- Each write to the firmware write-data register shall insert one 32-bit word into the pre-conditioner stage.
- If the pre-conditioner FIFO is full, the write shall not be accepted.
- A full status shall be exposed to firmware.
- A write to a full pre-conditioner FIFO shall also assert a recoverable alert.
- If firmware terminates the insertion sequence while the pre-conditioner FIFO is still full, a recoverable alert shall be asserted.

---

## 8. Entropy Conditioning

### 8.1 Standard Conditioning

When not in bypass mode:

- Post-health-test entropy shall be packed and fed into the SHA-3 based conditioner.
- The conditioner shall operate in SHA3-384 mode.
- The conditioner shall accept message data only when it is ready.
- The module shall coordinate the start, processing, and completion of each conditioning operation.
- When complete, the conditioner shall produce a 384-bit entropy word.

The module shall coordinate with the CSRNG halt interface during hash processing in order to limit power spikes. The halt request shall be asserted when hashing is about to begin and released after the hash operation completes or is acknowledged.

### 8.2 Bypass Conditioning

When in bypass mode:

- The SHA-3 conditioner shall be bypassed.
- Post-health-test entropy shall be packed directly into 384-bit seed words.
- If firmware insertion is active, firmware-written words may be packed into these seed words.

### 8.3 Pre-Conditioner FIFO

- A pre-conditioner FIFO shall hold 64-bit words ready for the conditioner or bypass path.
- The FIFO shall apply backpressure to the post-health-test stage when full.
- In standard mode, the FIFO shall be cleared when health tests are cleared.
- In firmware-insertion mode, the FIFO shall be cleared when the module is disabled, but any complete word already in the FIFO may be drained by the conditioner before the clear takes effect.

### 8.4 Conditioner Error Reporting

If the SHA-3 conditioner reports:

- Sparse state-machine error
- Count error
- Keccak storage reset error

the module shall report a fatal error condition. These errors shall also be visible through the fatal error interrupt and error-status registers.

---

## 9. Final Entropy Seed Storage

The module shall maintain a final entropy FIFO for complete 384-bit seed words.

Each final seed word shall include:

- A 384-bit entropy value.
- A FIPS compliance flag.

### 9.1 Final FIFO Enqueue

- A complete seed shall be enqueued when the final FIFO is not full.
- If the final FIFO is full, newly produced seeds shall not be enqueued.
- If the final FIFO remains full, subsequently produced seeds may be dropped without causing a fatal error.

### 9.2 Final FIFO Dequeue

The final FIFO shall be consumed by one of two paths:

- The software read path.
- The hardware entropy delivery interface.

Only one path shall be active at a time, based on the configured entropy routing.

### 9.3 Final FIFO Errors

The module shall report a fatal error if:

- A push is attempted while the final FIFO is full.
- A pop is attempted while the final FIFO is empty.
- The FIFO reports an inconsistent full/empty state.

---

## 10. Entropy Delivery to Software

When software entropy routing is enabled:

- Complete seeds shall be moved from the final FIFO into a software read packer.
- The software read packer shall convert 384-bit seeds into 32-bit words.
- The module shall expose an entropy-valid interrupt/status when at least one 32-bit word is available for firmware.
- Each read of the entropy data register shall return one 32-bit word and consume it.
- A full 384-bit seed shall be consumed after twelve 32-bit reads.

The software read path shall be active only when:

- The module is enabled.
- The OTP firmware-read enable is asserted.
- The entropy data register enable is asserted.

If the software read path is not active:

- The software read packer shall be held cleared.
- Reads from the entropy data register shall return zero.

If software consumption is slow, the software read packer may fill. When the packer is full, no further seeds shall be popped from the final FIFO. This backpressure may cause the final FIFO to fill, after which newly generated seeds shall be dropped.

---

## 11. Entropy Delivery to Hardware

When software entropy routing is disabled, the module shall deliver seeds through the hardware entropy interface.

The hardware interface shall provide:

- A 384-bit entropy seed.
- A FIPS compliance flag.
- Request/acknowledge signaling.

When a complete seed is available and a request is presented:

- The module shall place the seed on the 384-bit output.
- The module shall present the corresponding FIPS flag.
- The module shall assert the acknowledge indication.
- The seed shall be removed from the final FIFO.

The module shall not pop from the final FIFO when no valid request is present. A request made while the final FIFO is empty shall not be acknowledged until a seed becomes available.

If the final FIFO is empty and a hardware request is pending, the module shall wait until a conditioned seed is produced.

---

## 12. Bus Integrity Check

The module shall include a data-path integrity check to detect repeated entropy seeds.

For each pair of consecutive seeds delivered from the final FIFO:

- The module shall compare the low 64 bits of the current seed against the low 64 bits of the previous seed.
- If the two low 64-bit values are identical, the module shall assert a recoverable alert.

This check shall be active whenever the final FIFO is being consumed. It provides a statistical indication of possible entropy bus tampering or repeated data.

---

## 13. Interrupts

The module shall provide the following interrupts:

### 13.1 Entropy Valid Interrupt

- Asserted when software-readable entropy is available in the software read packer.
- Gated by the module enable.

### 13.2 Health Test Failed Interrupt

- Asserted when the health-test failure alert condition is raised.
- This occurs when the aggregate health-test failure count reaches the programmed alert threshold.

### 13.3 Observe FIFO Ready Interrupt

- Asserted when firmware-override mode is active and the observe FIFO depth reaches the programmed threshold.
- The threshold must be nonzero.
- The module must be enabled.

### 13.4 Fatal Error Interrupt

- Asserted when any fatal error condition is detected.
- Fatal error conditions include:
  - Input, observe, or final FIFO errors.
  - Acknowledgement state-machine errors.
  - Main state-machine errors.
  - Counter redundancy errors.
  - SHA-3 conditioner state or storage errors.

All interrupts shall support standard interrupt enable, state, and test behavior through the register interface. The interrupt output shall reflect the masked interrupt state.

---

## 14. Alerts

The module shall provide both recoverable and fatal alert outputs.

### 14.1 Recoverable Alert Sources

A recoverable alert shall be asserted for:

- Invalid multi-bit encoding of any security-sensitive configuration field.
- Health-test alert threshold reached.
- Main control state-machine alert.
- Entropy bus integrity check failure.
- Threshold configuration redundancy mismatch.
- Firmware-override write-to-full when insertion is enabled.
- Firmware-override disable with pending full condition.

The module shall also support a recoverable alert test input that causes the recoverable alert output to pulse.

### 14.2 Fatal Alert Sources

A fatal alert shall be asserted for:

- Any internal FIFO write, read, or state error.
- Acknowledgement state-machine error.
- Main state-machine error.
- Any counter redundancy error.
- SHA-3 conditioner state error.
- SHA-3 count error.
- SHA-3 storage reset error.

The module shall also support a fatal alert test input that causes the fatal alert output to pulse.

### 14.3 Alert Status Reporting

Recoverable alert source conditions shall be visible in the recoverable alert status registers. Fatal alert conditions shall be reported through the error-code registers and the fatal error interrupt.

---

## 15. Error Reporting

The module shall maintain error-code status registers that allow firmware to observe the source and type of fatal errors.

The module shall report:

- FIFO write errors.
- FIFO read errors.
- FIFO state errors.
- Acknowledgement state-machine errors.
- Main state-machine errors.
- Counter errors.
- SHA-3 state errors.
- SHA-3 storage reset errors.

When a fatal error source event occurs, the corresponding error-code status bit shall be set. The status shall remain set until cleared by firmware through the register interface.

---

## 16. Status and Debug Information

The module shall provide status information for firmware and debug tools.

This shall include:

- The current depth of the final entropy FIFO.
- The idle/busy state of the main control state machine.
- The current main state-machine state.
- Boot-phase completion status.
- SHA-3 conditioner state.
- SHA-3 block-processing status.
- SHA-3 absorption status.
- SHA-3 error status.

This information shall be read-only from the register interface.

---

## 17. Disable and Drain Behavior

When the module is disabled during normal operation:

- The RNG enable shall be deasserted.
- No new raw entropy shall be accepted.
- Health tests shall be cleared.
- The observe FIFO shall be cleared.
- The pre-conditioner FIFO shall be cleared in standard mode.
- The bypass FIFO shall be cleared.
- The final entropy FIFO shall be cleared.
- The software read path shall be cleared.
- No new seeds shall be delivered on the hardware entropy interface.

A disable request shall not cause spurious fatal errors solely because the data path is being cleared. The module shall remain safe to re-enable after the disable sequence completes.
